correctness.rationale: The independent bridge clock and exchangeable isolated-clique count process prove the exact Laplace law. Direct first-edge conditioning and a pure-death spectral calculation agree exactly in 72 graph-state and 588 Laplace comparisons. Each isolated clique ultimately leaves a uniformly placed single vacancy iff its size is odd, proving the weak-rate boundary. Maximal within-clique pairings prove the exact two-point jammed-size law. A density-dependent death-chain martingale limit and explicit expectation bound justify both logarithmic and rate-crossover limits. Independent finite calculations corroborate, but do not replace, these arguments.

value.rationale: A single rate-controlled intercommunity edge determines a parity-sensitive one-dimer gain or loss in an otherwise saturated dense two-community system. The theorem provides the exact bridge-event probability at all finite sizes and positive bridge rates, a weak-link singularity at odd order, a new logarithmic dependence on unequal community sizes and a nontrivial crossover when intercommunity attempts compete with O(a) hub-incident attempts. These are motivated physical/network transport features for irreversible adsorption, not arbitrary finite slices or known-table recomputations.
